summary: The main article describes a photoredox-catalyzed dicarbofunctionalization of styrenes using amines and CO2 to synthesize gamma-amino acids. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for both amines and alkenes, and mechanistic control experiments.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Typical approaches to γ -amino acid derivatives.
items.description: Comparison of literature methods (routes a-c) with the current work (route d) for synthesizing gamma-amino acids.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Photocatalytic preparation of γ -amino acids from CO2.
items.description: General reaction design showing the generation of alpha-aminoalkyl radicals and their addition to alkenes followed by CO2 capture.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions a
items.description: Screening of photocatalysts, additives, solvents, and concentrations to optimize the yield of product 3'aa.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Photocatalytic reactions of methyl 4-vinylbenzoate 2a with amines.
items.description: Substrate scope evaluation of various tertiary amines reacting with methyl 4-vinylbenzoate.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Photocatalytic reactions of methyldiphenylamine 1k and 1a with alkenes.
items.description: Substrate scope evaluation of various styrenes and alkenes reacting with amines 1k or 1a.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Control experiments for elucidation of the mechanism.
items.description: Mechanistic studies including isotope labeling, radical trapping with TEMPO/BHT, and radical clock experiments.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: The proposed reaction mechanism.
items.description: Proposed catalytic cycle involving reductive quenching of the photocatalyst, radical addition, and carbanion capture of CO2.
